# 1 Enoch Chapter 81 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)
**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Ge'ez MS; cf. 4QEn-astr (Aramaic) | **Section:** Astronomical Book (Book of Luminaries)

---

**1** He said to me: "Look, Enoch — these are the heavenly tablets. Read what is written on them, and note every detail."

**2** I looked at the heavenly tablets and read everything written there. I understood it all — it was the book of every human deed, the complete record of all the children of flesh who will ever live on earth, from the present to the farthest generations.

**3** At once I blessed the great Lord, the King of glory forever, who has made all the works of the world. I praised him for his patience and blessed him on behalf of all humanity.

**4** Then I said: "Blessed is the one who dies in righteousness and goodness — the one about whom no book of unrighteousness has been written, against whom no day of judgment will be found."

**5** The seven holy ones then carried me and set me down on the earth before the door of my house. They said to me: "Tell Methuselah your son everything, and make known to all your children that no human being is righteous before the Lord — for he is their Creator.

**6** We will leave you with your son for one year, until you have given your final instructions — teaching your children, writing it down for them, and testifying to all of them. In the second year, we will take you from their midst."

**7** "Keep your heart strong. The good will proclaim righteousness to the good; the righteous will rejoice together with the righteous and congratulate one another.

**8** But sinners will perish alongside sinners, and the apostate will sink down with the apostate.

**9** Those who practice righteousness will suffer on account of sinners' deeds, and will be removed because of what the godless do."

**10** When they had finished speaking, I returned to my people, blessing the Lord of the world.

---

*PNEUMA notes: Dynamic equivalence rendering. Chapter 81 is one of the most theologically dense in 1 Enoch. Enoch reads the heavenly tablets — the complete record of all human history — and is then sent back to earth for a final year. The declaration "no flesh is righteous before the Lord" (v. 5) parallels later Second Temple and Pauline theology. The seven holy ones are the seven archangels of the Book of the Watchers (chs. 20-21).*
